summary.title: Building A Simple AI Chatbot With Web Speech API And Node.js
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a browser voice chatbot that listens with SpeechRecognition, gets replies from API.AI via a Node.js server over Socket.IO, and speaks them back with SpeechSynthesis.
takeaways: Use SpeechRecognition (with webkit prefix in Chrome) to capture the user's voice and read the transcript from the result event.
Pass the transcript from the browser to a Node.js/Express server over Socket.IO, then fetch a reply from API.AI's Node.js SDK.
Use window.speechSynthesis and SpeechSynthesisUtterance to speak the server's reply aloud.
Speech recognition works only in Chromium-based browsers per the article; Firefox, Edge and Safari support only speech synthesis at the time of writing.
summary.summary: The tutorial by Tomomi Imura walks through building a voice chat interface in the browser. A Node.js server uses Express and Socket.IO, and the front end uses the Web Speech API to listen to speech and speak replies. Recognized text is sent to API.AI (a natural-language service, using its free small-talk preset) and the response is returned over the socket and voiced with speech synthesis. The article notes that speech recognition is only supported in Chromium-based browsers, while synthesis has wider support.
